newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia EU ratification session postponed.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia EU ratification session postponed.

text.p: Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said on Wednesday a parliamentary session to ratify an association accord with the European Union was postponed until next week to allow more time to reach broader agreement.
"After talks with representatives of the parliamentary parties, we agreed to postpone the session to next week," Drnovsek, leader of the centre-left Liberal Democrats, told a news conference.
"We will use this week to discuss the parties' positions towards joining the EU and changes to the constitution," he added.

The association agreement was signed in June last year. Under the terms of the accord, Slovenia agreed to change its constitution to allow foreigners to own property within four years of the association pact taking effect.
Drnovsek said he will ask the Constitutional Court to rule on whether ratification of the agreement without previous alterations to the law would contravene the constitution.
He said if the court decided that an immediate change to the constitution was necessary, it would significantly delay Slovenia's membership of international alliances.
Slovenia hopes to be included in the first wave of NATO expansion but such a ruling could also have an impact on entry into the alliance.

Slovenian President Milan Kucan earlier this week said fast ratification of the association accord was a precondition for the country's inclusion in the group of countries to start negotiations on full membership of the EU in 1998.
The parliamentary vote could also be held up by an attempt by a group of citizens who have demanded a referendum on ratification of the accord.
Under Slovenian law, 40,000 signatures are needed for a referendum to be proposed. If the proposal is accepted by parliament, then the referendum must be held.
